tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search jobs: find live job postings from employer career sites and job boards by role or keywords, place, remote work, employment type and pay. Returns up to 10 job cards a page; each card has fit (every applied filter as met, partial, unknown or not_met, and a verdict of match or near_match), posting (age, freshness, last seen live), an indexed pay amount when there is one (posted only when salary.salarySource is structured, provider, page_text or extracted; otherwise unconfirmed), and the employer's title and summary as source text. coverage says what was searched and whether more pages exist; for the next page, call again with continuationInput unchanged, which keeps the filters this search resolved, and page with offset only when it is absent. filters.jobTypes takes FULL_TIME, PART_TIME, CONTRACT or other listed types, any of which match; filters.salaryListedOnly keeps only jobs that list pay; filters.minSalary is annual pay in the requested currency, and ranges that overlap it are included. Licence requirements and eligibility are not assessed. For one posting use get_job, for more like a job find_similar_jobs, for one employer list_company_jobs, for counts get_market_insights or get_local_demand.

fallbackToVisitorPlace.description: When the query names no place and the search is not remote, search the signed-in person's saved country, or the country of an anonymous visitor's IP address.

variants.description: Up to 4 more wordings of the same search, such as other job titles for the same work. They run at the same time as query, with the same filters, radius, limit and page, and each counts as one search toward the search limit. Results come back in variants, one entry per wording, leaving out jobs already listed above them; repeatedJobIds names those. Use this instead of separate searches for alternative titles.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Get job: read one job posting in full by its id from search_jobs, list_company_jobs or find_similar_jobs: the job posting's employer description, requirements, pay when listed, location, job types and application link, plus posting (age, when Metaintro last saw it live, and closesAtLocal when the employer gives a closing time). Title, summary and description are employer source text; licence requirements and eligibility are not assessed. Use it to read a job posting's details before calling the job a fit; use find_similar_jobs when it is closed or not right.

tools.name: get_market_insights
tools.description: Summarize the job market for a role and place: a short explanation that gives the number of matching postings when a count is available and, when enough postings carry them, the median listed pay, the largest work arrangement and the top requested skills. groundedMetricKeys lists which of these figures the explanation contains; any figure it does not list is unavailable for this search. interpretation shows how the query was read. Takes a query and the same filters as the job search. Use it for market size and pay, not for the jobs themselves; get_local_demand fits when the person has no role in mind yet.

fallbackToVisitorPlace.description: When the query names no place and the search is not remote, search the signed-in person's saved country, or the country of an anonymous visitor's IP address.

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: Read an employer's profile by its slug (companySlug on a job card): what it does, size, headquarters, pay bands observed in its postings, work arrangement, benefits, recent events and hiring activity measured from the postings Metaintro tracks. A single field Metaintro has no data for is null; an empty list (workArrangement, benefits, technologies, recentEvents) means none were observed, not that the employer has none. hiring.definitions says what each hiring number measures: medianOpenPostingAgeDays is the age of open listings, not time to fill, and removedRoles30d counts postings taken down, not roles filled. Use it for how an employer hires and pays; use list_company_jobs for its open jobs.

tools.name: list_company_jobs
tools.description: List one employer's open job postings by its slug (companySlug on a job card), newest first, as compact cards with posting age and the employer's title and summary as source text. Pages are cut to fit the response size; continue with nextCursor until it is null. Use it when the person asks about a specific employer; use search_jobs to search across employers and get_job to read one posting in full.

tools.name: find_similar_jobs
tools.description: Find up to 10 open postings like one job, by its id: the same kind of role in the same place, or remote when the job is remote, as job cards. basedOn names the job they were matched to. Use it when a job is closed, a near miss, or the person wants more like it; use search_jobs when they describe what they want in their own words.

tools.name: get_local_demand
tools.description: Read which kinds of roles are hiring most in a place (city, region or country): open postings by role category, with total open postings, employers and sectors. When the place has too few role types it widens to the region, the country or worldwide; scope and locationLabel say which area the numbers cover. Counts are postings, not hires. Use it when the person does not yet know what to look for; use search_jobs once they have a role in mind and get_market_insights for one role's pay and size.

tools.name: verify_job_link
tools.description: Check whether a job from any link (Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor, an employer's careers page or applicant tracking system) is still listed by the employer itself. Looks the posting up in Metaintro's index of employer career sites and, when it is there, reads the employer's own posting page. status is open_at_employer (the employer's own posting page, matched by link or requisition id, reads as open), listed_open, closed, not_found, employer_not_tracked, needs_details (ask for employer and title, then call again) or could_not_check. Returns when it was checked, the matching Metaintro job with its links, and open roles at the same employer. Free; no sign-in.

url.description: The job link the person has, from any site.

employer.description: The employer's name, when the link does not show it (Indeed links never do).

title.description: The job title, when the link does not show it.
